purpose: A neon night drive: a cyan-lined highway to a glowing horizon under a starfield, a city with lit windows between two low-poly wireframe ranges, the striped sun climbing and setting behind the city with the day (night is only a glow), violet gates rushing over the road, an 80s wedge supercar modelled in 3D and seen through the floor's own camera, weaving and yawing ahead so its flank and roof show, lit violet as gates pass over it, its headlights pooling on the road ahead and its orange tail lights leaving trails and a faint reflection on the wet road, and the time in cyan segment digits above it all.

accent.where: the time digits, the one quantity; cyan also draws the road edges, lane dashes and wireframe ranges as scenery, while magenta, violet, orange and pink paint the rest of the scene

night.recipe: The lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes (the Vinyl precedent); the mat around it, visible on the square device, flips with --face-bg, and night dimming comes from the kiosk brightness. For a dark room the glow option pulls the halo in.

options.intent: full is the neon as designed; soft keeps the tubes and their white cores but pulls the halo in, the setting for a clock by the bed.

antiPatterns.rule: Never paint the neon or the stage with --face-ink or --face-bg
antiPatterns.why: the lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes, like the Vinyl record; the day ink is black and would vanish on it, so only the mat outside the disc reads --face-bg

antiPatterns.rule: Never draw the still parts live every frame
antiPatterns.why: nine glow passes per stroke made the drafts cost 17 to 20 ms a frame at 1080; anything that changes at most once a minute goes through N.layer in src/apps/clock/neon/faces/horizon.ts or the Pi drops frames

antiPatterns.rule: Never give the car a badge, a maker name or a plate
antiPatterns.why: the silhouette is a homage to the 80s wedge supercars; a logo would turn it into a trademark and pull the eye off the time

antiPatterns.rule: Never store the car trail as a history of past frames
antiPatterns.why: the trail is weave(t - d) re-projected d seconds closer, a pure function of time, so it survives a dropped frame, a pause and a remount without a jump

antiPatterns.rule: Never let the sun, the city or a gate reach the digits
antiPatterns.why: the time is the only quantity on the face; the sun tops out at y 370, the city at about 400 and gate bars stay under the horizon by construction (gate height below the eye height), all under the digits ending at 310

antiPatterns.rule: Never put text on the car plate or a sign in the scene
antiPatterns.why: the time is the only text the face carries; a plate or billboard word reads before the digits and is a brand waiting to happen

antiPatterns.rule: Never draw the car as a flat sprite or with its own perspective
antiPatterns.why: it is a mesh projected by the same camera as the floor (spread = F / Z), so its flank, yaw and size agree with the lanes and gates at every weave position; a second perspective would make it slide on the road

specless: Drawn on a canvas by src/apps/clock/neon/faces/horizon.ts in the shared 1000-unit space. A perspective grid, a striped sun and segment digits have no place in the spec vocabulary of solid hands and two tick rings, so the numbers live in the draw module.
